references.text: The Sabbath command is formally given in the Ten Commandments, where the Lord commands that the Sabbath be kept holy as a day of rest.
The Sabbath is described as holy to the Lord, and Israel is commanded to keep it as an everlasting covenant.
Moses repeats the Sabbath command to the people, including the prohibition against kindling fire on the Sabbath.
The Sabbath is referred to as a holy convocation and a day of rest (שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן).
A man who gathered wood on the Sabbath was punished, demonstrating the seriousness of the Sabbath command.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for trading and working on the Sabbath, reminding them of its holiness.
Isaiah speaks of calling the Sabbath a delight and honoring it by refraining from one's own pursuits.
Jesus discusses the Sabbath with the Pharisees and declares himself Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus says that the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
The women prepared fragrant spices but rested on the Sabbath according to the command, just as the Israelites were to prepare food the day before.
A direct continuation of the same event confirming the basis of the Sabbath law in God's provision.
